newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki resumes Nokia-fired rally, volume mighty.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki resumes Nokia-fired rally, volume mighty.

text.p: Encouraged by a low-inflation signal from the U.S., shares stormed to a strong close on Friday in heavy Nokia-led trade amid a late burst of buying which took volume up to mighty levels for Helsinki, brokers said.

Volume topped one billion markka, with bourse engine Nokia accounting for more than half, ending at 324.00 markka, up 16.50 or more than five percent with a boost from rallying U.S. tech stocks and short-covering by overseas investors.

The general HEX index was up more than one percent most of the day and jumped again to end 2.37 percent higher at 2,777.13 -- up 1.5 percent for the week -- after key U.S. data soothed fears that inflation might spur a U.S. rate rise. Some brokers said there could be more gains next week.
"We went clearly bullish as fears for a U.S. rate hike diminished after the data," one broker said referring to a GDP figure suggesting lower-than-expected fourth quarter inflation.

Paper machine group Valmet added 3.00 markka to close at 93.00, helped by the strong dollar and news that its Automotive unit would begin making Porsche cars. "I guess it's neat to own a company that builds Porsches," one said.
Forestries broadly underperformed, with UPM-Kymmene closing flat but up from lows.
Insurer Sampo ended 18.00 markka higher at 440.00 in heavy 40 million markka trade, catching up with recent rises in its archrival Pohjola.

Small caps added breadth to the rise. Fireplace maker Tulikivi surged more than 14 percent to end up 9.00 markka at 71.00 after reporting higher 1996 earnings and saying it saw good prospects for this year.
Engineering group Santasalo added 4.00 markka to 56.00, pursuing Thursday's gains after it said it would buy a cast component unit.
